title: WDAC POLICY REBASE
subtitle: APP CONTROL FOR BUSINESS
NEW BASELINE
NO RECOMMENDED BLOCK RULES
LOCAL · NO GPO
ROUTE A OR ROUTE B
description: The rebase replaces the App Control base policy on a PAW with a new Wizard baseline that has both Recommended Block Rules boxes unchecked, deployed locally without GPO. Steps 0 to 2 back up the device, take it out of GPO scope and build the new baseline. Steps 3 to 7 validate it and swap the base policy in Audit, either with a new GUID (Route A: remove the old policy, re-create its supplementals; every step documented by Microsoft) or by keeping the GUID (Route B: an undocumented XML edit, then an in-place replacement). Steps 8 and 9 capture every application again, merge and screen, then enforce and verify V-243450 and V-243451.

badge.text: Windows 11 22H2+ · unsigned policy · CiTool · PS 7 or 5.1

container.label: PAW being rebased
container.note: backup in C:\WDAC\Backups\Rebase-<timestamp> · scripts in C:\WDAC-Scripts · both block-list boxes unchecked

sections.label: Role
sections.text: Make the change reversible, take the device away from the GPO, and build the new baseline

sections.label: Step 1 · leave GPO scope
bullets: Move the computer out of the WDAC GPOs' OU
gpupdate: AppControl GPO and WDAC-GPO-Deploy task gone
The old .cip stays on the device until step 5 or 6

sections.label: Step 2 · Wizard
bullets: [Wizard] Allow Microsoft, Multiple Policy Format, Audit ON

bullets.text: Both Merge with Recommended Block Rules boxes UNCHECKED

callout.title: leave the GPO first
callout.text: A GPO still in scope redeploys its policy: Route A would end with two base policies, Route B gets replaced.

sections.label: Role
sections.text: Validate the new baseline and put it in place of the old base policy, in Audit

sections.label: Step 4 · validate (both routes)
bullets: 2 x WARN: no deny rules in scenario 12 / 131 = boxes unchecked

sections.label: Route A · new GUID · documented
bullets: 6: scripts 1 + 2 deploy the baseline, new GUID

sections.label: Route B · keep GUID · not documented
bullets: 3: write the old GUID into Base-Audit.xml (XML edit)
6: scripts 1 + 2 replace the policy in place

callout.title: route B step 3 is undocumented
callout.text: No cmdlet sets a chosen GUID. Microsoft recommends the Wizard or ConfigCI cmdlets over editing the XML.

sections.label: Role
sections.text: Capture every application again on the new baseline, then enforce when you decide

sections.label: Step 8 · audit cycle
bullets: Reboot, run EVERY app: earlier allow rules are gone

sections.label: Step 9 · enforce + verify
bullets: Reboot, approved apps run, block-test app gets 3077

callout.title: never merge the old reference
callout.text: The old Base-Enforce.xml and Base-Audit-Merged.xml hold the block rules. Merging them brings the rules back.

bar.label: Policy files
bar.title: New Base-Audit.xml (no block rules) → Base-Audit-Merged.xml → Base-Enforce.xml
bar.note: Old files stay in the Step 0 backup · after the swap, every revision keeps the new baseline's GUID and raises VersionEx

panel.label: Route choice + guardrails
panel.note: pick one route before step 3 · what keeps the rebase safe

banner.title: Route A (new GUID) or Route B (keep the GUID)
banner.sub: both end the same: one base policy in Audit, rebuilt, then enforced

cards.title: Route A · new GUID
cards.subtitle: documented · recommended
lines: Keep the Wizard's random GUID
Step 5: CiTool -rp the old base + supplementals
Step 7: supplementals re-created for the new base
Script 1 writes the new GUID to PolicyGuid.txt

cards.title: Route B · keep the GUID
cards.subtitle: fewer steps · not documented
lines: Step 3: old GUID into the new XML (XML edit)
Script 1 picks a HIGHER version: in-place swap
Supplementals keep working, PolicyGuid.txt unchanged
Tested: compiles in PS 7 and 5.1

cards.title: Leave GPO scope
cards.subtitle: step 1 · GPO README §10.3
lines: Move the computer object out of the WDAC OU
gpupdate removes the task; the .cip stays
Don't disable the GPOs: other devices use them

cards.title: Two boxes unchecked
cards.subtitle: §1.3 · the trade-off
lines: User mode: Microsoft-signed bypass tools now allowed
e.g. msbuild, mshta, wmic, wsl; -AllowWSL not needed
Kernel mode: Windows' own driver blocklist still on

cards.title: Read the mode first
cards.subtitle: §1.2 · before you start
lines: User mode (V-243451) gives the mode: 1 = AUDIT
Kernel mode often reads 2 from built-in policies
CiTool IsEnforced = True means active, not enforce

cards.title: Roll back
lines: Fastest: restore the Step 0 checkpoint
Enforced, need Audit: README §11 Option A
Back to GPO: A removes the new base; B needs a higher package

footer: C:\WDAC\config · app control for business · policy rebase · 2026
